blockers.title: Refresh token reuse breaks connections
blockers.whatToDo: Persist the new refresh token atomically and don't refresh in parallel. On invalid_grant, ask the user to reconnect.

blockers.title: Production redirect must be HTTPS
blockers.whatToDo: Use an https callback URL in the Production app.

evidence.claim: OAuth apps are created in Developer tools, with Sandbox and Production environments; a second Production app is recommended for real customer data
evidence.quote: Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.

evidence.claim: Token endpoint is https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token with Basic client authentication for server apps
evidence.quote: Send a POST request to Get Access Token at https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token.
Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method.

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 2 hours; refresh tokens don't expire until used; token request rate limit
Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate
evidence.quote: Each successful response from POST /oauth/token will still return a new access token and a new refresh token.

evidence.claim: Redirect URI rules differ between Sandbox and Production
evidence.note: Sandbox allows https and http on localhost. Production allows https only.

evidence.claim: Get current user endpoint is used to test the access token
evidence.note: The developer account page says to test with the Get current user endpoint. The path /users/me is from general knowledge.

review.note: Searched 'Calendly developer production OAuth app review go live' and the docs. Found no review or publishing page; docs only describe Sandbox vs Production app types.

token.note: Also read the refresh token rotation guide.

requirements.detail: You need a Calendly account (or sign-up) to open Developer tools.
requirements.label: Calendly account

requirements.detail: Every authorization request must include code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256.
requirements.label: PKCE S256

requirements.detail: Enter exactly one URI per app. Sandbox allows https and http on localhost. Production allows https only.
requirements.label: Redirect URI rules

requirements.detail: Server apps send client_id and client_secret with HTTP Basic auth. Always include client_id in the body.
requirements.label: Client authentication at token endpoint

requirements.detail: Store the new refresh_token from every refresh response and discard the old one.
requirements.label: Refresh token rotation

requirements.detail: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within 1 minute.
requirements.label: Token rate limit

scopes.note: At least one scope is required. The scope list page was not read.

points: Log in to Calendly or sign up.
Older accounts may still use developer.calendly.com.
steps.title: Sign in to Calendly Developer tools

steps.output: Client ID, client secret, webhook signing key
points: OAuth apps tab → Create OAuth app.
App name: letters, numbers, hyphens and spaces only.
Environment: Sandbox. Enter exactly one redirect URI.
Select at least one scope, then Create.
steps.title: Create a Sandbox OAuth app

where.label: Developer tools → OAuth apps → Create OAuth app

points: Copy all three values on the creation screen.
The secret and signing key can't be viewed again.
Paste them into your agent's secret store, with your OK.
steps.title: Save credentials in your app

points: Redirect the user to the authorize URL with a code_challenge.
POST the code to the token URL with code_verifier.
Use HTTP Basic client auth for server apps.
Overwrite the stored refresh token on every refresh.
steps.title: Implement authorize and token exchange with PKCE

where.label: Calendly API reference → Get Access Token

points: Create a second app with Environment type Production.
The redirect URI must be https; localhost is not allowed.
Swap the production client ID and secret into your app.
steps.title: Create a Production OAuth app

where.label: Developer tools → OAuth apps → Create OAuth app

points: Success is HTTP 200 with the user's resource and organization URIs.

points.text: Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate.
points.why: Access tokens last 2 hours. Each refresh returns a new refresh token, and reusing an old one fails with invalid_grant.

verdict.summary: Register a Calendly OAuth app yourself and choose the Production environment for real users. The docs I read describe no review step.
